recipes.name: Fluffy protein banana chocolate cake
recipes.desc: Soft banana-chocolate cake in an Auflauf form. Whipped egg whites make it fluffy, crème fraîche keeps the whey from drying it out, and it has very little added sugar.

steps.c: Heat the oven to 170 °C Ober-/Unterhitze (150 °C Umluft) and grease the form. Separate the eggs: whites into a large, clean, dry bowl (A), yolks into bowl B. Mash the bananas with a fork, melt the butter and let it cool, chop the chocolate (and walnuts). In bowl C stir the whey, flour, Backkakao, Backpulver and salt together with a spoon.
Beat on low for 30 s until foamy, then on high. At soft peaks add half the sugar a spoonful at a time. Beat until stiff and glossy, 3–4 min in total. Set aside.
Same beaters, no need to wash. Beat the yolks with the other half of the sugar and the Vanillezucker on medium for 2 min, until pale and thick.
Add the bananas, crème fraîche, milk and melted butter. Beat on medium for about 1 min until smooth. Now put the beater away.
Tip bowl C into bowl B and fold until no dry flour is visible. Stop there: overmixing makes it tough.
Stir a third of the whites into the batter to loosen it. Fold in the rest gently in two goes: cut down the middle, scrape along the bottom, turn the bowl. White streaks are fine.
Fold in about three quarters of the chocolate (and walnuts).

Fill the form about ⅔ full (3–4 cm of batter) and smooth gently. Scatter the rest of the chocolate on top and bake straight away, 25–30 min, until a skewer comes out with a few moist crumbs. Check at 25 min; cover loosely with foil if the top browns too fast.
Let it cool in the form for at least 20 min before cutting. It firms up as it cools.

recipes.notes: Walnuts: 40–50 g, toasted 3–4 min in a dry pan and chopped; then use 60 g chocolate. Small form (about 15–20 × 10–15 cm): make the full recipe and put the extra batter in muffin cases (bake 15–18 min), or use ½× with 1 banana and 1 large egg + 1 extra white. No crème fraîche? Use about 120 ml Schlagsahne instead of the crème fraîche and milk. Leaner: swap 100 g crème fraîche for Skyr or Magerquark. Best slightly warm, with unsweetened whipped Schlagsahne and a pinch of flaky salt. Not sweet enough? Add 15–20 g sugar or a drizzle of honey next time.

ing.name: Sugar (half for the yolks, half for the whites)

recipes.name: Protein muffins (Rührteig)
recipes.desc: Classic German Rührteig muffins with a quarter of the flour swapped for whey and less sugar. Full butter and extra milk keep them moist.

steps.c: Heat the oven to 175 °C Ober-/Unterhitze (155 °C Umluft). Put paper cases in the muffin tin.
Beat the soft butter with the sugar and Vanillezucker for 2–3 min until pale and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Mix the flour, whey, Backpulver and salt.

Stir the dry mix into the butter mix in two goes, alternating with the milk, only until combined. The batter should be soft and almost pourable, looser than a normal Rührteig; add another tbsp of milk if it is stiff. Let it rest 5 min so the whey can soak up the liquid.
Fill the cases about two thirds full. Bake about 18 min, until a toothpick comes out barely clean. Don't overbake: whey makes them dry.
Leave 5 min in the tin, then cool on a rack.

recipes.notes: With vanilla whey: use 70–80 g sugar and leave out the Vanillezucker. Never swap more than about a third of the flour for whey, or they turn dry and spongy. Add-ins that work: chopped dark chocolate, blueberries, a mashed banana (then 2 tbsp less milk).

recipes.name: High-protein baked cheesecake (Quark)
recipes.desc: Creamy German-style Käsekuchen with mostly Magerquark and a little Frischkäse on a crunchy oat base. High in protein and lightly sweet; the slow cool-down keeps it from cracking.
recipes.time: 20 min + 50 min baking + 1 h in the oven + 4 h chilling
recipes.pan: 20 cm springform (or a 20×20 cm form lined with baking paper)

steps.c: Take the Quark, Frischkäse and eggs out of the fridge 30–60 min before, so they are at room temperature (cold ones give lumps and cracks). Heat the oven to 160 °C Ober-/Unterhitze; not Umluft, which dries and cracks the top. Line the bottom of the springform with baking paper.
Blitz the oats briefly, or use them whole for more crunch. Mix with the melted butter and honey, press firmly into the form with the back of a spoon. Bake 10 min.

Beat the Frischkäse with the sugar, Vanillezucker and salt until smooth. Add the Quark, Speisestärke, lemon zest and juice and mix until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing only until each is just combined. Keep the beater on low the whole time: unlike the banana cake, you want NO air in a cheesecake, or it puffs up and cracks.
Pour the filling onto the base and tap the form on the counter twice to pop bubbles. Bake 45–55 min, until the edge is set and the middle still wobbles slightly like jelly when you nudge the form.
Turn the oven off, open the door a crack with a wooden spoon and leave the cheesecake inside for 1 hour. After the first 10 min, run a thin knife around the edge so it can shrink without cracking.
Cool to room temperature, then cover and chill at least 4 h, best overnight. It sets and slices cleanly only when cold.

recipes.notes: Small form (about 15–20 × 10–15 cm): use ½× with 2 eggs and bake about 35–40 min. Cracks are only cosmetic; cover them with berries. Topping: warm frozen berries with a little honey, or a thin layer of Skyr with vanilla. More protein: use Skyr instead of Frischkäse (a bit firmer and tangier). With vanilla whey you can swap 20 g of the Speisestärke for 30 g whey and leave out the Vanillezucker, but it gets firmer.
